family.tagline: A house lined with books, a lake out back and one Companion Core.
family.story: Sally runs a small consultancy from the library, with the Companion Core on its writing desk. John writes software in the primary suite, Steve plays upstairs and Jean studies at her own desk. The lake is just out the back.

home.lede: A cascade of brick gables sits under a dark shingle roof, with twin chimneys. A white-columned porch waits at the top of the front steps. The ground floor is open and lined with books, and the pool garden runs down to the lake.

spots.line: Bookcases along the walls, a grand piano and the Core on its writing desk.
A bistro table, two Windsor chairs and a fireplace.
A writing desk with a laptop, a loveseat, a fireplace and a telescope.
A breakfast bar with three stools, where the week’s dinners get planned.
Jean’s desk sits under a lamp, beside her single bed and dresser.

day.line: Monday starts under the library clock, with the admin hour.
John opens the book catalogue at the writing desk.
Lunch at the breakfast bar settles the week’s dinners.
A client signs at the bistro table before the school bus.
Sally corrects a date and sends the reply herself.
Jean writes her paragraph first and checks it after.
Steve plays upstairs while the session runs in the library.
Saturday afternoon fills both chesterfields for the lake video.
By the pool, two phones play the same audiobook.

members.name: Sally
members.work: consultant, runs her own small practice

companion.name: Juniper
companion.job: Drafts replies to Sally’s clients from the notes she sends it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Sally reads and sends every message.

profile.bio: Sally runs a small consultancy from the library. Her week, her client folders and the letters they sign sit on the Core, and Juniper drafts replies that she reads before they go.

companion.name: Quill
companion.job: Drafts home automation rules and notes from what John types to it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. John reads every word before it is used.

profile.bio: John writes software from the primary suite and keeps a catalogue of the library’s books as a side project. His editor and the house manual sit on the Core, and Quill drafts his rules.
Steve plays on the Core from his desk upstairs, with his own Valve account. His phone pictures land on the Core, and he treats bin day as a quest.
Jean writes her French first and checks it after, keeps her books, comics and PDFs on one shelf, and saves her sources. Each tool she uses does one job on the Core.

chapters.title: By the pool and the lake

popup.title: A parcel waits up the steps
popup.body: Up the front steps, Jean finds the parcel on the porch. John carries it through the chess hall to the library, where Sally has cleared the writing desk.

popup.title: Steve lifts out the Companion Core
popup.body: Steve lifts the Companion Core onto the writing desk. Jean lays the power cable, the quick-start guide and the recovery USB drive out on the rug.

popup.title: Plug it in beside the lamp
popup.body: Steve plugs the Core in by the desk lamp, and Jean presses the button. It wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Joining the Core from Jean’s phone
popup.body: Jean joins the Core’s own network from her phone’s Wi-Fi settings. Then she picks the home network.

popup.title: Hermes first, then two apps
popup.body: Sally browses the Companion Hub store from the writing desk and picks Hermes. The family adds Companion Planning and Nextcloud, then walks away.

popup.title: Sally names her agent Juniper
popup.body: Sally names her agent Juniper and sends a first message. A reply comes back, the Core beside her.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Hello, Sally. I am Juniper. Where shall we begin?

detail.before: Sally typed each reply to a client herself, and kept the reminders in her head.
detail.after: Juniper runs in its own sandbox on the Core. Sally texts it a few lines and reads the draft that comes back.
steps: Pick Hermes in the Companion Hub store
Give the agent a name
Send it a first message
detail.fact: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: A double scan, split before sending
popup.body: One scan holds two clients’ papers. Sally splits it in Stirling-PDF on the Core, so each client gets only their own pages.

detail.before: Splitting a scan meant uploading the whole stack to Smallpdf, including the pages that belonged to the other client.
detail.after: Stirling-PDF splits the scan on the Core. Each client’s pages become their own file before anything is sent.
steps: Open the scan in Stirling-PDF
Split it where the second client starts
Save one file per client
detail.fact: Stirling-PDF merges, splits, compresses and converts PDFs on your own Core.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: Monday’s admin hour comes first
popup.body: Monday’s admin hour used to be whatever the client calls left over. Now Sally blocks it first in Companion Planning, one local file on the Core.

detail.before: Client calls sat in one calendar, school dates in another, and Monday’s admin hour nowhere at all.
detail.after: Companion Planning keeps tasks and time blocks in one local file on the Core. Sally places the admin hour first, then the calls.
steps: List the week’s calls and deadlines
Block the admin hour first
Fit the school dates around it
detail.fact: Companion Planning plans tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core. Briefings from a local model are optional.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: The last client folder comes home
popup.body: Sally copies her last client folder out of a rented drive. Nextcloud on the Core now holds all five years of folders, filed by surname like the shelves behind her.

detail.before: Client folders sat in Dropbox, with the client contacts kept in a separate app.
detail.after: Nextcloud holds the folders and the contacts together on the Core, synced to Sally’s devices.
steps: Copy the last folder to the Core
File each client by surname
Open a folder on a laptop or phone
detail.fact: Nextcloud keeps your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: One word finds the piano’s receipts
popup.body: One word, tuning, brings up the grand piano’s receipts. Paperless-ngx reads and tags each page, so the whole lot is searchable.

detail.before: Receipts went into Evernote as photos, and the tuner’s invoice was somewhere among them.
detail.after: Paperless-ngx reads each page on the Core, tags it and files it, so one word finds the invoice.
steps: Scan the stack of receipts
Check the tags Paperless-ngx chose
Search for the word tuning
detail.fact: Paperless-ngx scans and files your paperwork: it reads every page, tags it and makes the lot searchable.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Sally fixes a date, then sends
popup.body: Sally changes one date in Juniper’s draft, then sends the reply herself. Juniper drafts on the Core’s local model, from three lines Sally typed at the piano stool.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Here is the draft. Please check the dates before it goes.

detail.before: A moved deadline meant opening the mail window, finding the thread and writing the apology from a blank page.
detail.after: Sally texts Juniper three lines. Juniper drafts the reply on the Core’s local model, and Sally reads it, fixes it and sends it herself.
steps: Text Juniper three lines
Read the draft and fix what is wrong
Send the reply herself
detail.fact: Hermes is an agent built for messaging: it connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app.

beats.capability: fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core

popup.title: Signed at the chess hall table
popup.body: A client from next door climbs the steps and signs on Sally’s laptop at the chess hall table. The signed letter stays in Docuseal on the Core, no inbox involved.

detail.before: Signing meant sending the letter to DocuSign and waiting for the client to open an email.
detail.after: Docuseal runs on the Core. The client signs at the table, and the signed PDF stays on the Core.
steps: Open the letter in Docuseal
Turn the laptop to the client
Keep the signed PDF in the folder
detail.fact: Docuseal fills and signs PDF forms on any device, from your own Core.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Saturday’s film stars the family
popup.body: Saturday’s film is John’s lake video from four summers back. Steve picks it from a list of nothing but the family’s own files, and Jellyfin streams it from the Core.

detail.before: The family’s home videos played through Plex on the television.
detail.after: Jellyfin streams the same files from the Core to the TV, and everyone picks from one list.
steps: Open Jellyfin on the TV
Pick the lake video from the list
Press play
detail.fact: Jellyfin streams the movies, TV and music you already have to the devices in your home.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: Four people, three stools, one planner
popup.body: Four people share three stools at the breakfast bar, so the week needs one place. Dinners, shopping and dentist visits live in a Yuvomi planner on the Core.

detail.before: Dinners were on a note, the shopping on a phone and the dentist on a wall calendar.
detail.after: Yuvomi keeps dinners, shopping and the calendar in one planner, stored in a database on the Core.
steps: Plan the week’s dinners
Add what is missing to the list
Put the dentist on the calendar
detail.fact: Yuvomi is a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals, notes, contacts and budget in one app.

beats.capability: turn habits and chores into a game with levels and quests

popup.title: Bin day is a quest now
popup.body: Steve takes the bins out because bin day is a quest he set up himself. Habitica, running on the Core, turns the chore list into a game.

detail.before: Chores sat in a Todoist list that nobody opened after Tuesday.
detail.after: Habitica turns the same chores into quests with rewards, and the game runs on the Core.
steps: Add bin day as a quest
Take the bins out
Tick it off and collect the reward
detail.fact: Habitica turns habits and chores into a game with levels and quests.

beats.capability: write code in VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core

popup.title: The editor follows John around
popup.body: John’s book catalogue no longer lives on one laptop. Code Server keeps it on the Core, so the editor tab follows him to the loveseat.

detail.before: John wrote the book catalogue in Cursor, with the project folder on that one laptop.
detail.after: Code Server opens the editor in a browser tab on the home network, with the project folder on the Core.
steps: Open the editor in a browser tab
Open the project folder on the Core
Carry on from any room
detail.fact: Code Server runs VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core.

beats.capability: chat with models running on your own Core, in a browser

popup.title: Where John’s stack trace goes
popup.body: A test fails in John’s book catalogue, so he pastes the trace into Open WebUI. The model on the Core answers, and he reads it before changing a line.
popup.note: A model on the Core can be wrong.

detail.before: John pasted error traces from his side projects into ChatGPT whenever a test failed.
detail.after: Open WebUI sends the trace to a model on the Core. John reads the explanation and changes the code himself.
steps: Paste the stack trace into Open WebUI
Read the explanation against the code
Change the code himself
detail.fact: Open WebUI chats with models running on your own Core, in a browser.

beats.capability: write a wiki or a set of manuals in books, chapters and pages

popup.title: What only John knows, written down
popup.body: John writes down how the house runs, as a book in BookStack on the Core. Sally can search any page, and every page keeps its history.

detail.before: The family’s how-to notes sat in a Notion page that only John could find his way around.
detail.after: BookStack keeps the manual as books, chapters and pages on the Core. Search finds a phrase, and each page keeps its history.
steps: Start a book for the house
Add a chapter for the Core
Write a page, then read its history
detail.fact: BookStack writes a wiki or a set of manuals in books, chapters and pages, with search and history.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: The session runs in the library
popup.body: Upstairs, Steve signs in to his own Valve account. The session itself runs on the Core in the library, and he plays it in a browser.

detail.before: A cloud gaming service such as GeForce Now runs the session on its own servers and streams it to the player.
detail.after: Steam Headless runs the session on the Core, and Steve plays it in a browser in his room.
steps: Sign in with his own Valve account
Open the Steam library in the browser
Pick a game and play
detail.fact: Steam Headless runs Steam on your Core and plays it in a browser on a screen in the house.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Steve’s pictures join everyone else’s
popup.body: Steve’s phone sent every picture to Google Photos. Now, on the home Wi-Fi, they back up to Immich on the Core, beside everyone else’s.

detail.before: Steve’s phone uploaded every picture to Google Photos, and the whole summer sat in that account.
detail.after: Immich takes the pictures onto the Core and gathers them into one family collection. Its first start takes a while.
steps: Install Immich from the Companion Hub store
Sign in on the phone while at home
Let the first backup finish
detail.fact: Immich backs up, searches and organises your family photos and videos on your own Core.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: The check comes after the writing
popup.body: Jean writes the lake paragraph in French herself. Then she pastes it into LibreTranslate on the Core and compares the result with what she meant.

detail.before: Jean checked her paragraphs by pasting them into Google Translate.
detail.after: LibreTranslate runs on the Core. Jean writes first, pastes second, and compares the result with what she meant to say.
steps: Write the paragraph by hand first
Paste it into LibreTranslate
Compare the result with what she meant
detail.fact: LibreTranslate translates text and documents on your own Core, and your words are not sent to a third party.

beats.capability: manage and read books, comics and PDFs with automatic covers and metadata

popup.title: Comics and school PDFs, same shelf
popup.body: Jean’s comics and school PDFs no longer live apart from her ebooks. BookLore keeps them on one shelf on the Core, with covers and details added from the internet.

detail.before: Jean read in a Kindle account, with her comics and school PDFs kept in other places.
detail.after: BookLore keeps the ebook files, comics and PDFs the family has on one shelf on the Core, with covers and details added from the internet.
steps: Add an ebook, a comic and a PDF
Check the covers BookLore found
Open any of them from the shelf
detail.fact: BookLore manages and reads books, comics and PDFs, with automatic covers and metadata.

beats.capability: save web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot

popup.title: The page as Jean read it
popup.body: The page Jean quoted has changed since she read it. Her Linkwarden copy, a screenshot and a PDF, is the page as she read it.

detail.before: Jean saved her essay sources as bookmarks in Raindrop.io, and the pages themselves stayed out on the web.
detail.after: Linkwarden saves each page with a screenshot and a PDF on the Core, so Jean can still read a source as it was after the page changes.
steps: Open the source page
Save it in Linkwarden
Open the saved copy later
detail.fact: Linkwarden saves web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot.

beats.capability: turn text into natural speech on your own Core

popup.title: Jean hears her essay read aloud
popup.body: Jean has Kokoro read her essay aloud, so she can hear where the sentences run long. The voice is made on the Core, from her own text.

detail.before: Jean proofread by re-reading in her head, which skipped the clumsy sentences.
detail.after: Kokoro turns her essay into speech on the Core, and Jean follows the page while it plays.
steps: Finish the draft
Have Kokoro read it aloud
Mark each sentence that runs long
detail.fact: Kokoro turns text into natural speech on your own Core.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: John reads the pump rule first
popup.body: The pool pump’s plug had two timers, in two apps. John’s agent, Quill, drafts one rule, and John reads and saves it in Home Assistant on the Core.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: john
say.text: Here is the rule. Please read it before you save it.

detail.before: The pump’s plug answered to its maker’s app and to Google Home, each with its own timer.
detail.after: Home Assistant on the Core holds one schedule for the plug on the home network, and John reads Quill’s draft rule before he saves it.
steps: Describe the pump hours to Quill
Check each line of the drafted rule
Save it in Home Assistant
detail.fact: Home Assistant controls and automates your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account.

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off

popup.title: Two loungers, one audiobook, two bookmarks
popup.body: Two loungers can share one audiobook, because Audiobookshelf remembers where each listener stopped. By the pool, two phones play files the family already has, kept on the Core.

detail.before: Audiobooks played through the Audible app, and each listener’s place in the story was kept there.
detail.after: Audiobookshelf organises the audiobook files the family already has on the Core and remembers where each listener stopped.
steps: Add the audiobook files to the library
Press play on a phone by the pool
Pick up from the same place later
detail.fact: Audiobookshelf organises audiobooks and podcasts and remembers where each listener stopped.

popup.title: One Core among the books
popup.body: From the library to the pool, one Companion Core serves the house, and the shelves are still lined with books.

closing.body: Sally’s client folders, John’s code and Jean’s sources sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and choose your first apps.

notes: suite-code is the one code-server beat and keeps the owner’s sign-off: content/story/reviewed.json lists it (slug brennan, rule app-qa-screenshot). Its service is Cursor, as in the signed-off beat.
Told in the v3 shape: sixteen of twenty room beats are pairs. The four pair-less beats are Companion Planning, the Hermes draft, Yuvomi and Kokoro; none of them replaces anything in the catalog.
Jean is fourteen: no chat model and no agent in her beats (age rule 16). Open WebUI is John’s beat. LibreTranslate, BookLore, Linkwarden and Kokoro are tools that do one job.

The Nursery is a spare room and never a stage: Steve’s anchors use desk/kids nth 1 and room/kids nth 2, Jean’s use nth 0. No beat anchors on a bed. living-sign is the chess hall bistro table (patio-seat, room living, nth 0).
Steam Headless: Valve account named, no frame rate, no title, home network only. Docuseal: the client signs in person at the chess hall table, and nothing is said about the signature itself.
Home Assistant: the pump is a plug on the home network, no energy claim. Quill and Juniper reach the family through the chat service they pick, and the Hermes beats carry that note.

One beat per app: the first-run greeting (ftue-hello) is an agent beat with no app, so Hermes has one story beat (office-draft). Nextcloud and Companion Planning are named in ftue-pick only as the first installs.
